name: Rae Villa
life: “I still remember recovering a real invitation from the kitchen bin.” Monday often includes a stop at Ferris Deli, where Rae asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I threw out the letter as a joke. The post carrier came back after work to tell me it counted.
appearance: Rae has an aquiline nose and a square chin. Look for brown hair pinned away from the temples. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a cropped bottle-green coat with a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges. In conversation Rae turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Rae uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Rae well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To recover the real invitation before the closing date.
family: Judith Dai is Rae’s older cousin. Rae checks the date twice. Judith brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *The late crossing*, Judith says, “I work in traffic planning. I brought the ride log to the meeting that was going to cut another late bus.”
connections: Clara Baines. A discarded envelope is proof that a missed deadline began with a plausible mistake.

reactions.response: Rae puts distance between the frightened person and the argument and asks nearby staff for help.
